I will keep this year simple and manageable. I am 75, and some people in my family work off-farm, so I will not spread labor too thin or chase risky high-input production. Since I have 14 mu and already follow a wheat-maize system, I will keep most of the land in that familiar rotation because I know it well, it fits my irrigation conditions, and it gives steady grain for the household and cash income. I will put 10 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 4 mu in cotton because cotton still gives me another source of income, but I do not want too much of it because it needs more spraying and more hands. I will use better seed on all three crops because I want stable emergence and yield, but I will not push fertilizer to extremes. With well irrigation, I will water at the key stages instead of too often. I will also keep tillage practical: rotary or plough where I need a good seedbed, and no-tillage for maize after wheat to save time and labor. My goal is steady output, lower labor pressure, and fewer surprises.
